name: Azarel
overview: Azarel was a male leader from the tribe of Dan who served as the chief officer for the Danites. He is noted in Scripture as the son of Jeroham. His role as a chief officer highlights his position of responsibility within his tribe during the time recorded in 1 Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The name Azarel means 'G-d has helped,' reflecting a theologically significant meaning rooted in the Hebrew name El for God. This proper name was not given directly by God but carries a reminder of divine assistance.
familyAndRelationships: Azarel is explicitly identified as the son of Jeroham. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not record any additional family connections for Azarel.
scriptureSignificance: Azarel's significance lies in his leadership role within the tribe of Dan as their chief officer, indicating a trusted and authoritative position in the organization of Israel during the period chronicled. His mention in 1 Chronicles 27:22 emphasizes the structured governance among the tribes under King David's administration, underscoring the importance of faithful service in God's people.
